answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because signal only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, quill is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any voyage approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
